names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 28 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Ευστράτιος ο Νηστευτής ο Οσιομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 28 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Преподобни мученик Евстратије Печерски.“, with both rank words left off — Преподобни and мученик, which are what this folder's `venerable-martyr` carries. Печерски is kept: it is not a rank but the by-name the heading gives him, of the Caves, and a bare Евстратије would fold with `eustratius-of-mount-olympus`.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 28ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Ευστράτιος ο Νηστευτής ο Οσιομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The page records the relic — «Το Λείψανο του Αγίου βρίσκεται αδιάφθορο στη Λαύρα των Σπηλαίων του Κιέβου», incorrupt in the Lavra of the Caves of Kiev — and describes how he is painted on the icons: light hair, a thin beard, the monastic habit, and barefoot. It dates the Polovtsy raid «Στις 20 Ιουλίου του έτους 1096 μ.Χ.» and gives no year for the crucifixion itself. It prints no hymn. This is a Russian saint recorded here only from a Greek source.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 10.04.2026 (28. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни мученик Евстратије Печерски.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Greek already keeps in this folder, and the same monk of the Caves: sold into slavery to a Jew at Korsun after the raid, the fast unto death the captives chose together rather than apostatise, the fourteen days he lasted alone, the crucifixion, the spear, the body thrown into the sea and floating. **It dates the raid 1097 where this folder holds 1096, and that year is `attested`** — saint.gr gives 20 July 1096 — so nothing was touched and the disagreement is recorded here; displacing an attested year is the author's call and not a reader's. The stored form keeps Печерски, the by-name the heading gives him, of the Caves; a bare Евстратије would fold with `eustratius-of-mount-olympus`, which holds that form. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Στις 20 Ιουλίου του έτους 1096 μ.Χ., η Λαύρα των Σπηλαίων του Κιέβου, έγινε ξαφνικά στόχος επιθέσεως των Πολόφσκυ» — the year of the raid that carried him off. The page gives no year for his crucifixion, which its own narrative puts six years and some weeks later, and none is inferred here.
